rejected_videos.reason: No clean, technically accurate standalone segment meets this concept's needs. The technical-feasibility discussion at 242–316 seconds briefly identifies technology constraints, but its example contains material factual errors: at 298–312 seconds it characterizes WAV quality as inadequate and claims heavily compressed MP3 audio loses no quality. Lossy MP3 compression does discard audio information; WAV is a container that commonly holds uncompressed PCM audio, not inherently inferior-quality audio. Trimming before these claims leaves an incomplete example and only partial coverage of f1. The video does not teach the PM/engineering division of responsibilities (f2), questions about dependencies, uncertainty and effort (f3), or distinguishing hard constraints, manageable risks and scope-cost tradeoffs (f4). The surrounding material predominantly concerns product positioning, usability and commercial viability rather than a PM-depth engineering feasibility conversation.

No clean standalone segment teaches the intended PM-depth feasibility conversation. The feasibility section at 75–121 seconds discusses system design, load estimates, staffing, and budget, but does not explain the PM/engineering division of responsibilities (f2) or distinguish hard constraints, manageable risks, and cost–scope tradeoffs before adjusting a proposal (f4). Extending the range introduces hardware/software co-design, hardware partitioning, and API-wrapper implementation beyond the path's allowed knowledge rather than supplying those missing facts. The video's categorical demands to prove feasibility and finalize requirements before any coding also obscure the uncertainty and iterative tradeoffs central to this lesson.

The cleaner selection-and-goal passage at 439–511 depends on the previously calculated budget and does not explain PO preparation, Product Goal alignment, or a product briefing. Extending through implementation planning adds task-board and engineering details without supplying those missing PO facts.

The opening at 646–699 cleanly explains that the event is not a management status report, but does not establish the 15-minute Developer event or the PO-as-Developer participation condition. Reject for a materially inconsistent calculation: at 178–200, monthly item counts are presented as column-level performance and used to identify development as the slowest column; at 244, development's four items per month are multiplied by four developers to obtain 16 items per month, while subsequent calculations reinterpret the other column counts as per-person rates.
